articles.title: Netanyahu Erupts At Mamdani: ‘Tormenting His Own Voters’ As NYC Mayor Calls For ICC Arrest
articles.description: Benjamin Netanyahu has accused New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani of “tormenting his own voters” as their confrontation over Gaza and the ICC arrest warrant against the Israeli prime minister intensifies. Mamdani has declared Netanyahu unwelcome in New York, described him as a war criminal and urged the US federal government to act on the warrant. After a legal review, however, the mayor acknowledged that New York City lacks independent authority to arrest Netanyahu. The Israeli leader responded by accusing Mamdani of condemning Israel while excusing Hamas and Iran—allegations the mayor denies. The ICC issued warrants for Netanyahu and former defence minister Yoav Gallant in 2024 over alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity in Gaza. Israel rejects the charges, while Donald Trump has promised Netanyahu will not be arrested anywhere in the United States. Watch.

articles.title: Burnham Appointee Under Fire Over 2010 Hamas Meetings, Gaza Trip Ignites Crisis For New UK Govt
articles.description: Andy Burnham’s newly appointed solicitor general, Andy Slaughter, is facing scrutiny over meetings with Hamas-linked politicians during fact-finding visits to the Palestinian territories in 2010. According to The Telegraph, Slaughter travelled with Jeremy Corbyn and met Palestinian figures associated with Hamas, as well as representatives of rival faction Fatah. During a separate Gaza visit, he also met officials serving in the Hamas-run administration. Slaughter later argued that peace required engagement “without preconditions,” including negotiations with Hamas. Such meetings were not illegal at the time: Britain had proscribed Hamas’s military wing but did not outlaw the organisation’s political wing until 2021. The Attorney General’s Office rejects claims that Slaughter sympathises with Hamas, saying he has consistently condemned the group, supports a two-state solution and will perform his duties impartially. Watch.

articles.title: Pro‐Saudi militias launch major attack on Houthis in Marib & Al‐Jawf
articles.description: Heavy fighting has erupted in northern Yemen as clashes intensified between Houthi fighters and Saudi-backed forces across Al-Jawf and Marib provinces. According to Press TV and Yemen TV, airstrikes targeted Houthi reinforcements, missile launchers, Katyusha rocket sites, and weapons depots in several frontline districts, including Al-Jubah, Al-Safra, and Majzar. Reports also claimed that several Houthi fighters, including missile specialists, were killed during the latest operations. The escalation follows recent Houthi threats to target Saudi-linked commercial shipping in the Red Sea and enforce a maritime ban near the Bab al-Mandab Strait, raising fresh concerns over regional security.

articles.title: Big Political Attack: Yogi Adityanath Targets Previous Governments in Mainpuri Rally
articles.description: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, while addressing a public gathering in Mainpuri, launched a sharp attack on previous governments and highlighted the achievements of the BJP-led double-engine government. He accused earlier regimes of creating insecurity for farmers, traders, women, and youth, alleging that corruption affected employment opportunities. Yogi said that under the current government, recruitment processes have become transparent and young people from districts like Mainpuri and Etawah are receiving appointment letters based on merit. He claimed that Uttar Pradesh has moved from being considered a “BIMARU” state to becoming a revenue-surplus state and one of India’s leading economic contributors. The Chief Minister emphasized that there is no shortage of funds for development projects, including roads, stadiums, museums, auditoriums, connectivity projects, and public facilities. He also highlighted schemes for farmers, youth, women, and poor families. Referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision, Yogi said the government’s focus is on four key groups — the poor, farmers, women, and youth — and their empowerment will help India become a developed nation.

articles.title: Political Storm: Jantar Mantar Protest Ends, Political Battle Continues
articles.description: The Jantar Mantar protest may have ended, but political tensions continue. New Education Minister Prahlad Joshi has taken charge and held his first meeting with officials. Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi has intensified his attack on the government by writing a letter to Home Minister Amit Shah over the police action during the July 20 student protest. Rahul questioned who ordered the lathi charge and the use of pellet guns against students. He also asked whether people seen in plain clothes during the action were police personnel or volunteers, and who authorized their deployment. The resignation of former Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan has triggered a political credit war, with Congress claiming Rahul Gandhi’s pressure forced the government’s decision. Congress has demanded accountability from Amit Shah and shared videos of the police action. The BJP has rejected these allegations. BJP leader Tarun Chugh accused Rahul Gandhi of using youth issues for political gains and said Congress has no genuine concern for students’ future. The issue is expected to create further clashes between the government and opposition in Parliament.
